brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume

priceAsk.summary: Ask for price in the ₹0.65–0.80/pc range if we commit higher volume or relax spec
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — so there's room to move down.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — no reason to loosen terms given the quality issues

brief.financialLeverage: This supplier publishes no financials, so we can't see their profit, debt or how tight their cash is. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is small — we're not a big customer driving their revenue. That means we lean on lining up a strong second source and on their own quality trouble: 40% of deliveries get returned, which is expensive and risky for them. Push on price and quality together, but don't squeeze so hard that a fragile supplier walks away — we need reliability more than a few rupees saved if quality stays broken.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate. Health score B (65/100), revenue ₹2569.83 Cr — strong and proven.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable — a robust alternate for bottles/closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded & blow-moulded packaging; broad capability across bottles/caps.

risks: The 40% return rate is a red flag — if quality and paperwork don't improve fast, every delivery will cost us time and money in rework and delays.
We have no visibility into their finances, so we don't know if they're stable or struggling — watch for signs they can't invest in fixing the quality problem.
Our ₹1.66 L spend is tiny to them — they may not prioritize our fixes or price asks unless we dangle volume or make the quality pain clear.
Pushing too hard on price before quality is fixed could make them cut corners further or walk away, leaving us scrambling for supply.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to keep working together, but 40% of your deliveries are coming back — let's fix that first, then talk about better pricing if we can grow the volume.
